notice: Feasibility research, not an offering memorandum or investment recommendation. Costs are USD planning allowances unless a source is explicitly identified. Sites A and B are working parcel matches derived from the active project because the supplied Prospects token pages could not be machine-read; confirm the exact link-to-parcel mapping before relying on them. No contractor bid, environmental clearance, horse purchase, insurer approval or customer commitment is verified.

sources.title: FBi Buildings · stall systems
sources.note: About $4,500 for a standard 12 × 12 ft stall. Twenty implies $90,000 for stall systems, not a completed barn. Layout affects the price; Indiana supplier, not a Carolina bid.

sources.title: Morton Buildings · stall-barn planning
sources.note: Site preparation, ventilation and layout require design. No numeric local construction quote established.

sources.title: Zareba · fence cost comparison
sources.note: Wood three/four-rail reference: $5–10 per installed linear foot. Not a current Carolina bid. Steel and hybrid model rates below are independent planning allowances, not quoted here.

sources.title: USPA · rules
sources.note: Arena playing surface: 300 × 150 ft; outdoor field: 300 × 160 yards. Neither includes support land, runoff, parking or horse facilities. Review current rules with the designer.

sources.title: NC General Assembly · agricultural definitions
sources.note: Horse boarding is included in the agricultural definition. This does not automatically qualify an event venue, all improvements, or an ownership entity for preferential taxation.

sources.title: NCDOR · 2022 horse-boarding amendment
sources.note: Horse boarding added for tax years beginning on or after July 1, 2022. Older guidance excluding boarding must not control the analysis.

sources.title: NC General Assembly · PUV qualifications
sources.note: Agricultural qualification generally requires 10 acres in actual production and a three-year average gross income of $1,000, plus ownership/management conditions and exceptions. Parcel size alone is insufficient.

sources.title: Mecklenburg County · FY2027 budget
sources.note: FY2027 county rate: 49.27 cents per $100 taxable value, or $4,927 per $1 million. This excludes municipal/district rates and fees and does not apply to other counties.

sources.title: York County · real-estate tax formula
sources.note: SC tax uses taxable value × assessment ratio × mills / 1,000. Six percent is the ordinary non-primary-residence real-estate ratio. Do not reuse the PDF’s example millage as today’s rate.

sources.title: SC General Assembly · Chapter 43
sources.note: Agricultural use and entity-specific ratios need review. Section 12-43-220(d)(4) describes rollback for the change year and three preceding qualifying years; an older York application still says five. Current statute takes precedence.

sources.title: UMN Extension · horse care on a budget
sources.note: Preventive veterinary care, feed quality, biosecurity and emergency provision belong in the budget. Rations depend on body weight, forage tests and workload; quantities below are costing assumptions, not feeding instructions.

sources.title: UMN Extension · hoof care
sources.note: Summer trimming/shoeing commonly every 6–8 weeks; performance horses may need more frequent attention. Six-week model cycle is provisional; obtain a polo-experienced farrier’s plan.

sources.title: NC Cooperative Extension · Coggins clinic
sources.note: Clay County clinic listed $25 Coggins, $150 dental float including sedation and $45 six-month health certificate. These are historical discounted event rates, not full-service Charlotte farm-call costs.

sources.title: Tractor Supply · compressed alfalfa
sources.note: Standlee compressed alfalfa, approximately 50 lb: $29.49 shown, about $0.59/lb. Delivered bulk hay can price differently. Tax, shipping, availability and bale weights need confirmation.

sources.title: Tractor Supply · concentrate feed
sources.note: Purina Strategy Healthy Edge, 50 lb: $27.99 shown, about $0.56/lb. A price comparator, not a recommendation that every polo horse receive this ration.

sources.title: Tractor Supply · bedding reference
sources.note: Related-item panel displayed fine pine shavings, 5.5 cu. ft., at $6.49. Bag usage varies with turnout, absorbency and stall cleaning; volume is not compressed-bale mass.

sources.title: Triangle Area Polo · lessons
sources.note: North Carolina operator offers introductory assessments, group learning and member practices on club or privately owned horses. Covered lighted arena supports its year-round program. No price or demand is inferred.

sources.title: Virginia Polo · facility
sources.note: Facility describes a 300 × 150 ft lighted outdoor arena with irrigation for dust control. Arena irrigation is separate from drinking water.

sources.title: BLS · Charlotte regional wages
sources.note: Farm/ranch animal workers: $16.12 mean hourly wage in 2023. This is not a 2026 skilled polo-groom quote. Model uses higher editable wages and separate payroll burden.

sources.title: 4252-1 Reid Rd · current land listing
sources.note: 32.8 acres, $725,000, CMLS 4213472, RUD-1, parcel/parent ID 6130000014, well needed. The Prospects token itself could not be read, so confirm the supplied link resolves to this parcel.

sources.title: 4252 Reid Rd · 58.84-acre parent tract
sources.note: Parent tract is 58.84 acres and is marketed as two proposed tracts with seller-paid surveying after a tract goes under contract. Listing describes a flowing stream to a small southwest pond. The proposed 32.8-acre boundary therefore needs a final survey.

sources.title: York County · current equestrian zoning standards
sources.note: Current code applies special standards to equestrian uses and requires at least five acres. The use table treats commercial equestrian uses as conditional in rural/agricultural districts; the full polo/event/hospitality program needs a written zoning determination.

sources.title: SC Commerce · 156-acre Mixed-Use Lando Site
sources.note: Parcel 133-00-00-033-000, R-2, 156 acres, 140 listed developable acres, 420–500 ft elevation, 2.5 miles to I-77. Water is about 50 ft away via a 12-inch line; an 18-inch force sewer is listed about 1,600 ft away. Fishing Creek borders about 4,000 ft; a gas transmission line crosses the property.

sources.title: Chester County · current zoning ordinance
sources.note: R-2 lists agriculture, livestock production, ranching and equestrian uses as permitted. That does not by itself establish approval for ticketed polo, large spectator events, corporate hospitality, food/alcohol, lighting or amplified entertainment.

sources.title: Lando / Fishing Creek · broker topo and floodplain map
sources.note: Shows a broad 100-year floodplain corridor associated with Fishing Creek and interior lowlands plus mapped wetland/riparian screening. Listing materials say uplands above the 100-year floodplain are about two-thirds of the tract. Confirm with current FEMA data, survey and wetland delineation.

sources.title: USFWS · National Wetlands Inventory limitations
sources.note: NWI is a biological wetland inventory and does not establish regulatory jurisdiction. Any disturbance near mapped or suspected waters/wetlands needs appropriate agency and field review.

sources.title: SCDES · groundwater use reporting
sources.note: Outside designated Capacity Use Areas, wells or well systems using over 3 million gallons in a month must be registered. SCDES equates that threshold to roughly one inch of irrigation per week over 28 acres.

sources.title: SCDES · surface-water withdrawals
sources.note: South Carolina's surface-water withdrawal program applies above 3 million gallons in any one month. Stream or pond frontage should not be treated as unrestricted irrigation rights.

sources.title: SCDES · private and public well permitting
sources.note: Irrigation wells require the applicable Notice of Intent/general-permit process. A well serving potable water to multiple households or a small business is treated as a public water supply well and follows separate water-supply permitting.

sources.title: USGS · Piedmont and Blue Ridge aquifers
sources.note: Piedmont crystalline bedrock has little primary porosity; groundwater is stored in regolith and fractures. Reported yields vary greatly, with broad regional averages around 15–20 gpm. This is not a parcel well-yield estimate.

sources.title: SCDNR · South Carolina State Water Assessment, Chapter 6
sources.note: Historic compilation reports York wells averaging about 206 ft deep and 19 gpm, and Chester/Cherokee about 192 ft and 16 gpm. Local fracture conditions dominate; a test well/pump test is still required.

sources.title: SC General Assembly · current rollback-tax statute
sources.note: When qualifying agricultural real property changes to a nonagricultural use, Section 12-43-220(d)(4) applies rollback tax for the change year and the three immediately preceding qualifying tax years, subject to statutory provisions.

sources.title: Chester County GIS · SSURGO hydric soil layer
sources.status: Official county GIS / USDA-NRCS-derived soil layer
sources.note: Layer exposes map-unit name, surface texture, depth to water table, flooding class, drainage class, hydrologic group, slope, hydric rating and farmland class. Exact parcel AOI map units have not yet been extracted into this model.

sources.title: 1700 Westbrook Rd · current listing
sources.note: 156 acres, $2,106,000, My State MLS 11873124, parcel 1330000033, Fishing Creek frontage and $471 listed annual tax. The Prospects token itself could not be read, so confirm the supplied link resolves to this parcel.

fields.label: Total stalls
fields.note: Minimum brief. Includes owned, quarantine/visitor and boarding allocation.

fields.label: Club-owned horses
fields.note: Minimum purchase string; not a full string for 20 concurrent players.

fields.label: Quarantine / visitor reserve
fields.note: Do not sell these stalls as permanent board.

fields.label: Barn gross floor area
fields.note: Prototype footprint for stalls, aisle and services; designer must validate.

fields.label: Barn shell / foundations / erection
fields.note: Planning allowance, not a local bid. Excludes stall systems, utility package, separate storage and guest facilities. Material sales tax assumed within installed allowance.

fields.label: Stall fronts / partitions / mats
fields.note: Budget for complete stall fit-out; reconcile mats and partitions in quote. $4,500 supplier reference is dated and layout dependent.

fields.label: Outdoor arena package
fields.note: 300 × 150 ft playing surface plus engineered base, drainage, walls, footing and dust-control package. No roof. Local design/bid needed.

fields.label: Site preparation outside arena
fields.note: Clearing, grading, stormwater and erosion outside the arena package. Rock, wetlands mitigation and major retaining walls remain unpriced risks.

fields.label: Barn utilities / water / septic
fields.note: Electric service, plumbing, well or connection, fire-water and septic allowances. Guest restrooms are in guest package; reconcile shared septic scope.

fields.label: Driveways / parking / access
fields.note: Trailer turning, accessible parking, entrances and basic lighting. Road widening or major offsite work not priced.

fields.label: Guest pavilion / public restrooms
fields.note: Simple permitted experience facilities; no full restaurant, luxury clubhouse, lodging or wedding ballroom.

fields.label: Separate feed / hay / equipment storage
fields.note: Dry feed, safe hay storage and equipment shelter; do not duplicate barn storage in bid.

fields.label: Pasture establishment / shelters
fields.note: Soil testing, seed, drainage around turnout and modest run-ins; not a regulation grass polo field.

fields.label: Total fence length
fields.note: Prototype only: boundary plus internal divisions. Replace with measured layout, not acres converted to an assumed fence perimeter.

fields.label: Wood installed fence allowance
fields.note: Current planning band above dated supplier reference; rail count, labor, posts and coatings require quote.

fields.label: Steel installed fence allowance
fields.note: Planning allowance only; no local steel bid obtained. Specify coatings, welds, horse-safe geometry and installation.

fields.label: Hybrid steel proportion
fields.note: Hybrid uses this share of footage in steel, balance wood. Gates priced separately.

fields.label: Gates / hardware / paddock water
fields.note: Separate line; reconcile water lines with utility package. No barbed wire in the proposed horse areas.

fields.label: Tractor / mower / drag / trailer / tools
fields.note: Purchase allowance, not lease plus purchase. Include safe towing solution, maintenance equipment, manure tools and contingency transport.

fields.label: Suitable trained horse purchase
fields.note: Unsourced planning range. Obtain individual beginner-safe polo-mount evaluations, trial terms, age/history and purchase quotes. Not elite tournament values.

fields.label: Prepurchase exam / transport / intake
fields.note: Veterinary exam, targeted diagnostics, transport and intake. Verify tax/title/import costs as applicable.

fields.label: Tack / helmets / boots / mallets
fields.note: Saddles, bridles, protective equipment and shared learner kit. Fit/replace per instructor and insurer requirements.

fields.label: Design / permits / professional fees
fields.note: Architect, civil, geotechnical, permit and project-management allowance; legal acquisition costs are separate.

fields.label: Construction contingency
fields.note: Unknown-site risk reserve; not proof the scope is complete.

fields.label: Preopening hiring / training / launch
fields.note: Preopening payroll, marketing and systems only; post-opening payroll is operating expense.

fields.label: Construction carrying / finance fees
fields.note: Provisional construction interest, insurance/taxes before opening and financing fees. Replace with monthly draw schedule and actual holding period.

fields.label: Opening liquidity reserve
fields.note: Full fixed operating costs plus debt service for selected months; compare with forecast burn. Unknown taxes excluded until entered.

fields.label: Grass hay purchased ration
fields.note: Costing input only; alfalfa is another component, not a second complete forage ration. Pasture feed credits not assumed.

fields.label: Delivered grass hay allowance
fields.note: No local delivered hay quote obtained. Weigh bales; test forage and model waste.

fields.label: Alfalfa component
fields.note: Budget component; veterinarian/nutritionist must set the actual ration.

fields.label: Alfalfa price
fields.note: Base rounded retail comparator; do not treat as contracted delivered bulk hay.

fields.label: Concentrate / grain component
fields.note: Not a feeding prescription; grain, balancer and forage must be reconciled for each horse.

fields.label: Concentrate price
fields.note: Base rounded from $27.99 / 50 lb retail snapshot.

fields.label: Purchased forage wasted
fields.note: Delivered forage required = consumed forage / (1 − waste). Applies to grass and alfalfa, not grain.

fields.label: Bedding usage
fields.note: Turnout and cleaning dependent; not a universal husbandry standard.

fields.label: Bedding price
fields.note: Retail reference; compare exact bag size and delivered cost.

fields.label: Farrier / shoeing allowance
fields.note: Local polo farrier quote outstanding; corrective shoeing and emergency visits can exceed this.

fields.label: Farrier interval
fields.note: Lower-cost case uses eight weeks; must never replace individual care requirements.

fields.label: Routine vet / vaccines / dental / tests
fields.note: Includes farm calls, vaccines, dental, fecal-guided parasite control, Coggins and certificates. Historical discount-clinic fees are not sufficient.

fields.label: Emergency medical provision
fields.note: Expected-cost budget, not an insured maximum. Maintain emergency liquidity and decide major treatment policy with veterinarian/insurer.

fields.label: Brushes / hoof picks / fly protection
fields.note: Replacement brushes, combs, hoof picks, fly masks, fly spray, first-aid consumables, salt/minerals. New tack is startup; replacements are reserve.

fields.label: Drinking / wash water allowance
fields.note: Budgeting only, not a drinking-water limit; arena irrigation is in utility operating allowance.

fields.label: Variable water cost
fields.note: Marginal water/sewer or pump treatment allowance, not Charlotte tariff. Fixed connection/service charges belong to utilities.

fields.label: General manager / founder replacement pay
fields.note: Budget paid commercial leadership even when founder performs the role.

fields.label: Head trainer / polo instructor
fields.note: Dedicated role, separate from grooms and manager; actual schedule and qualifications to validate.

fields.label: Groom / barn staff equivalents
fields.note: 2,080 paid hours per FTE; coverage roster must account for seven-day care, leave, weekends and illness.

fields.label: Groom wage
fields.note: 2026 planning allowance; historical BLS occupational average is not a skilled polo-groom quote.

fields.label: Employer burden / relief allowance
fields.note: Payroll taxes, workers compensation, benefits and relief coverage; verify worker classification and actual premiums.

fields.label: Insurance allowance
fields.note: Obtain written polo/lessons/events coverage: liability, care/custody/control, property, umbrella, commercial auto and mortality/medical choices. Payroll workers comp counted in burden.

fields.label: Fixed utility / arena water / fuel
fields.note: Electricity, arena irrigation, fixed water/septic service and fuel. Marginal horse drinking/wash water counted separately.

fields.label: Routine facility / fence / field repairs
fields.note: Mowing, fence painting, footing care, pest control, routine equipment repairs. Major replacements are a separate cash reserve.

fields.label: Manure / waste removal
fields.note: Verify composting, runoff controls and hauling schedule; not free disposal.

fields.label: Sales / marketing / customer acquisition
fields.note: Annual fixed selling budget; measure cost per acquired paying guest and repeat rate.

fields.label: Legal / accounting / software / licences
fields.note: Ongoing administration and affiliations, booking systems, security, phone and licences; verify sales-tax treatment.

fields.label: Horse / tack / equipment replacement reserve
fields.note: Cash reserve below operating result. Includes retirement/replacement needs; not depreciation or routine care.

fields.label: Annual player dues
fields.note: Unverified price. Does not include unlimited club mounts or separately charged lessons.

fields.label: Net spectator admission
fields.note: After included/free tickets and sales taxes; do not count social-member included visits again.

fields.label: Net lesson / introductory experience
fields.note: Unverified realized price, before card fees and direct costs; model is for a supervised slot, not an unrestricted match.

fields.label: Incremental lesson delivery costs
fields.note: Consumables/extra hired help; permanent payroll and ordinary horse care are already fixed costs.

fields.label: Full-care board price
fields.note: Price unverified. Owner retains responsibility for separately billed vet/farrier unless contract says otherwise.

fields.label: Boarding feed / bedding / supplies
fields.note: Incremental boarded-horse care. Do not apply owned-horse annual vet costs a second time. Shared staffing capacity must be verified.

fields.label: Corporate package realized price
fields.note: Unvalidated B2B demand, not a signed booking. Only mounted participants count against horse-session capacity.

fields.label: Corporate direct delivery costs
fields.note: Catering, rentals, casual staff, clean-up and vendor fulfilment; model net of sales taxes.

fields.label: Private / partner event realized price
fields.note: Simple permitted event, not an assumed wedding venue. No lodging/restaurant sales included.

fields.label: Private event direct costs
fields.note: Includes vendor, setup/teardown and incremental staffing allowances.

fields.label: Match-day delivery cost
fields.note: Officials, medical/event safety, sanitation, casual staff, logistics and clean-up; scope requires event-specific quotes.

fields.label: Sponsorship fulfilment cost
fields.note: Recognize signed sponsorship only in an investment case; donated/restricted funds are not included.

fields.label: Payment / booking fees
fields.note: Conservative processing allowance on all revenue, including dues and board.

fields.label: Operating weeks
fields.note: Economic capacity input; not all-year demand proof.

fields.label: Healthy available string
fields.note: Allows for rest, illness and horse suitability; not a veterinarian-approved workload standard.

fields.label: Intro slots per available horse
fields.note: Provisional low-intensity scheduling units. High-intensity chukkers require a separate string/workload plan.

fields.label: Instructor-led sessions
fields.note: One staffed session; preparation, cool-down and rest must fit the roster.

fields.label: Maximum novice riders per session
fields.note: Provisional supervision assumption subject to instructor and insurer approval.

fields.label: Outdoor cancellations / lost sessions
fields.note: Higher-cost preset is not automatically a downside-demand case. This factor reduces completed outdoor activity.

fields.label: Bookable event dates
fields.note: Shared calendar for matches, corporate and private events; setup/teardown must fit.

fields.label: Included club-horse slots per player
fields.note: Consumes capacity but is not separately billed. Players with private strings require separate boarding/visitor planning.

fields.label: Mounted guests per corporate event
fields.note: Other guests may watch or do unmounted activities; no unlimited group riding assumed.

fields.label: Land closing / acquisition allowance
fields.note: Title/legal/survey/transaction allowance; rollback and exceptional land costs entered separately.

fields.label: Opening term debt
fields.note: Zero is an explicit all-equity illustration, not committed financing. Enter lender-backed amount.

fields.label: Term-loan rate
fields.note: Illustrative only, not a financing quote; fixed fully amortizing schedule.

fields.label: Amortization term
fields.note: No balloon/refinance assumed. Construction interest separately budgeted.

fields.label: Annual realized price growth
fields.note: Illustrative escalation, not market forecast; no land appreciation or exit value.

fields.label: Annual expense growth
fields.note: Applies to fixed and variable costs. Does not imply revenue growth keeps pace.

diligence: Address, parcel IDs, owner, asking price, acreage, deed, easements, covenants, survey and a broker availability check.
Actual gate-to-Uptown route along I-77 south, intended weekday/weekend departure times, traffic range and dated route evidence. Maximum target: 45 minutes.
Topographic survey, contiguous usable flat footprint, slope, soils, drainage, floodplain/wetlands, arena, paddocks and optional grass format drawn to scale.

Written county/planning determination for commercial polo instruction, boarding, spectators, hospitality, events, food/alcohol and any noise/light limits. Agricultural tax status is not zoning approval.

Paid pilots, repeat visits, member deposits, corporate letters of intent, event conversion, willingness to pay and actual contribution after labor/vendor costs.
Lender term sheet, development schedule, contingency, downside liquidity, runway, ownership/governance and clear separation of club funds, charity funds and investor distributions.

facts.label: Identity / acquisition
facts.finding: 32.8 acres at $725,000; RUD-1; CMLS 4213472. Listing uses parcel/parent ID 6130000014.
facts.implication: Land basis can be modeled, but parcel-level taxes and environmental geometry should wait for the final tract survey.

facts.label: Survey / title
facts.finding: The 58.84-acre parent is marketed as proposed tracts; the parent listing says surveying follows a tract going under contract. The individual listing also flags subdivision/other restrictions.
facts.implication: Require draft plat, title commitment, all restrictions/easements and a written right to terminate if the polo/event plan conflicts.

facts.label: Topography / flatness
facts.finding: No stamped topo or measured contiguous flat polo footprint has been verified for the proposed 32.8-acre boundary.
facts.implication: Do not credit a grass-field layout or low grading cost until the boundary and topo are overlaid with arena, barn, paddock, access, stormwater and parking.

facts.label: Surface water / drainage
facts.finding: The parent-tract marketing describes a flowing stream and a small pond in the southwest; the 32.8-acre listing itself says no waterfront.
facts.implication: The proposed split could materially change which drainage features are inside Site A. Confirm with survey, FEMA/NHD/NWI screening and field delineation.

facts.label: Soils
facts.finding: No exact SSURGO map-unit inventory has been established for the final proposed tract.
facts.implication: Extract the surveyed AOI in Web Soil Survey, then test arena/barn/parking subgrades, seasonal water, infiltration and any septic areas. County-wide soil labels are not acceptable substitutes.

facts.label: Groundwater
facts.finding: Listing says a well is needed. Piedmont groundwater occurs primarily in weathered regolith and bedrock fractures, so sustained yield varies sharply by well location.
facts.implication: Make a test well, sustained pump test and water-quality panel a feasibility condition. Historical York averages are context only, not a promised yield.

facts.label: Wastewater
facts.finding: No sewer is listed.
facts.implication: Public event restrooms, barn washwater and staffing can turn septic capacity into a site-layout constraint. Obtain a soils/site evaluation and written wastewater concept before fixing guest capacity.

facts.label: Water regulation
facts.finding: Irrigation wells require SCDES process; a small-business potable well can enter public-water-supply permitting. Groundwater systems over 3 million gallons/month require the applicable state registration/permit path.
facts.implication: Separate potable/fire demand from irrigation demand and model peak-month use, not annual average.

facts.label: Zoning / experience uses
facts.finding: York's current code regulates commercial equestrian uses as conditional uses in rural/agricultural districts and imposes equestrian standards.
facts.implication: Ask York County to classify polo instruction, boarding, ticketed matches, corporate events, food/alcohol, lighting, amplified sound and parking separately; 'horses' in a listing does not approve the whole business plan.

facts.label: Tax
facts.finding: A $339,480 assessment appears on the listing record, but the 32.8-acre tract still shares the parent parcel identifier.
facts.implication: Do not use that number as post-split or post-build taxable value. Obtain assessor treatment, agricultural-use eligibility and rollback exposure for the actual ownership/use plan.

facts.label: Environmental
facts.finding: No specific contamination finding was established in this desktop search.
facts.implication: Still obtain a Phase I ESA plus wetlands/flood/geotech work; absence of a search hit is not environmental clearance.

facts.label: Identity / acquisition
facts.finding: 156 acres at $2,106,000; parcel 1330000033. SC Commerce identifies TMS 133-00-00-033-000, unincorporated Chester County, R-2.
facts.implication: The land basis is modelable; use the TMS form for title/GIS work and confirm the current listing contract package.

facts.label: Developable area / relief
facts.finding: SC Commerce lists 140 developable acres and elevations from 420 to 500 ft. Listing narrative says uplands above the 100-year floodplain are about two-thirds of the tract.
facts.implication: 140 'developable' acres is not 140 flat polo acres. Draw the arena/grass/paddock/parking program on actual contours before assigning grading cost.

facts.label: Floodplain / wetlands
facts.finding: Fishing Creek borders roughly 4,000 ft. The broker topo/FEMA sheet shows a broad 100-year floodplain through the creek and interior lowland corridor, with wetland/riparian screening marks.
facts.implication: Keep permanent buildings, critical utilities and primary polo surfaces on verified uplands unless engineering/permitting proves otherwise. Obtain current FEMA data and field wetland delineation; NWI/broker maps are screening only.

facts.label: Soils
facts.status: official layer found; parcel extraction pending
facts.finding: Chester County's USDA-NRCS-derived SSURGO layer exposes map-unit name, texture, depth to water table, flooding, drainage class, hydrologic group, slope and hydric rating, but exact parcel map units have not yet been captured into the model.
facts.implication: Overlay the entire parcel, then field-test the candidate arena, grass field, barn, parking and septic/utility areas. Engineered polo footing/rootzone can differ from native soil.

facts.label: Potable / fire water
facts.finding: SC Commerce lists Chester Metropolitan District water about 50 ft away with a 12-inch primary line.
facts.implication: Get a current will-serve/capacity letter, pressure/fire-flow test, tap/extension fees and meter/backflow requirements. Distance to a line is not capacity.

facts.label: Sewer
facts.finding: SC Commerce lists an 18-inch force sewer about 1,600 ft away even though consumer listings summarize the property as having municipal sewer.
facts.implication: Do not model sewer as on-site. Obtain connection point, capacity, easement, pump/force-main scope, fees and construction cost before using public-event restroom assumptions.

facts.label: Fishing Creek / water use
facts.finding: Creek frontage is a resource but not an unrestricted irrigation entitlement. South Carolina regulates surface withdrawals above 3 million gallons in a month.
facts.implication: Quantify arena and grass irrigation by peak month. If creek withdrawal is contemplated, obtain SCDES classification/permit guidance and engineering for intake, low-flow conditions and water quality.

facts.label: Groundwater alternative
facts.finding: A separate irrigation well remains technically possible, but Piedmont well yield depends on fractures and local regolith. Historic Chester/Cherokee well yields average about 16 gpm in the cited state assessment.
facts.implication: Do not use the historical average as design capacity. Test-well and pump-test any groundwater alternative; register/permit high-volume use as applicable.

facts.label: Gas pipeline / easements
facts.finding: A natural-gas transmission line crosses the property. A 30-ft deeded access easement serves the easternmost portion.
facts.implication: Pull the recorded easements and operator requirements before orienting fields, buildings, parking or event circulation. No-build/setback and crossing requirements can reduce apparently usable acreage.

facts.label: Zoning / events
facts.finding: Current R-2 ordinance lists equestrian uses as permitted, but SC Commerce itself describes broader development as subject to Chester County zoning approvals.
facts.implication: Obtain written classification for commercial polo instruction, boarding, spectator events, corporate hospitality, food/alcohol, lighting/sound and event frequency. Equestrian permission alone is not the experience-center approval.

facts.label: Adjacent land use / environmental
facts.finding: SC Commerce identifies heavy industrial land use immediately west and the tract has prior timber-road use plus a gas transmission corridor. No specific release/contamination finding was established in this desktop search.
facts.implication: Prioritize a Phase I ESA, pipeline/title review and creek/wetland reconnaissance. Do not infer contamination from industrial adjacency, but do not ignore it either.

facts.label: Tax / rollback
facts.finding: The current listing reports about $471 annual tax, while the site is currently unimproved. That is not a credible post-development polo/event tax budget.
facts.implication: Have the assessor model ordinary vs qualifying agricultural value, improvements, business personal property and rollback. Current SC law uses the change year plus three preceding qualifying years for rollback, subject to statute.
